feedback: Written before this robot has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. (1) Evidence from iteration 4 (entityR2B): narrowing wheel_track to 0.10 m, with the iteration 1 array and controller, reduced the oval finish rate from 1.0 to 0.95, the s-bend finish rate from 0.40 to 0.15, and raised s-bend line_loss_events to 0.95. Iteration 1 (entityR2B) is the best measured layout: oval 20/20, s-bend 8/20, slalom 0/20 at progress 0.18. So the narrow track reduced stability, and the wider direction is the untested one. (2) I kept the iteration 1 controller unchanged, with no kp rescale for the wider track. Turn authority per unit of controller output scales with 1/wheel_track, so the 0.14 m track gives about 14 percent less turn rate per unit. Iteration 3 (entityR2B) shows that raising kp alongside a geometry change confounded the result and hurt every track, so I did not rescale. (3) Body_width has no effect on the off-track limit at 0.12 m (the 0.06 m floor governs), so it is not a lever. (4) Sensor x and y were not changed; iteration 3 showed the wider 20 mm array was harmful. Change rules for the next race: if the oval still finishes 20/20 and s-bend finish rate rises above 0.40 or line_loss_events falls below 0.8, try wheel_track 0.16 m next. If the s-bend finish rate falls below 0.40 or slalom progress drops below 0.18, turn authority is limiting, so return to wheel_track 0.12 to 0.13 m and then try kp scaled by 0.14/wheel_track only as a separate test. If the oval steering_oscillation stays near 0.25 and the oval finishes 20/20 but s-bend is unchanged, the track is not the lever, and the next geometry test should be sensor y at 0.065 m with the iteration 1 array.
requested_changes: Try wheel_track 0.16 m next if the 0.14 m race shows the s-bend finish rate above 0.40 with oval finish holding at 1.0, because iteration 4 showed narrowing the track hurt (s-bend 0.15, iteration 1 0.40), so the wider direction is the test of H1.

If the 0.14 m race shows the s-bend finish rate below 0.40 or slalom progress below 0.18, return to wheel_track 0.12 to 0.13 m, since the iteration 1 layout is the best measured and the loss of turn authority would be the limit.

If track width alone does not move s-bend or slalom, try sensor y = 0.065 m with the iteration 1 array and x = +/-0.024 m, since iteration 3 showed widening x is harmful but forward offset has not been tested.
